chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from one of our companions from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them).
Regarding the man who gives charity, is it permissible for him to inherit it? He said: Yes.

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: One of the two (referring to the 5th or 6th Imam)

ai.seo_question: Can a person inherit the charity they previously gave away?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the legal status of *sadaqah* (charity) in Shia jurisprudence, specifically addressing whether the donated item remains the donor's property for inheritance purposes. The Imam’s affirmative ruling indicates that unless specified otherwise, the act of giving does not sever the donor's ownership rights entirely, allowing the item to revert to his heirs upon his death. This distinction is crucial for understanding the flexibility of charitable endowments (*waqf*) versus simple gifts in Islamic law.
